messages.text: Brundle: Debating the rule that cost Norris and why Madring needs changes

metadata.summary: The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers.
metadata.content: Martin Brundle's verdict on Madring's F1 debut, the areas to change for 2027 and Virtual Safety Car rules | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Opinion Martin Brundle's verdict on Madring's F1 debut, the areas to change for 2027 and Virtual Safety Car rules Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle delves into the talking points from the Spanish Grand Prix, assessing F1's newest venue and where it can be improved, the debate around the rules that cost Lando Norris, and Kimi Antonelli's ever-growing world championship lead Martin Brundle Expert Analyst @MBrundleF1 Monday 14 September 2026 16:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player See how Lando Norris lost the lead and a likely win at the Spanish Grand Prix after an untimely Virtual Safety Car for the McLaren driver The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers. It all had a feeling of work in progress. We know they lost a lot of time in the build process with particularly bad weather, and as a temporary race track adjacent to the international airport, and effectively racing around the Madrid equivalent of the Birmingham NEC, it had its challenges. The pitlane and paddock were simply vast, creating some logistical challenges for all and, much more importantly, the track layout was not conducive to overtaking, to say the least. The event uniquely requires players to begin and finish every leg on a double or the bullseye. messages.text: McCullum: I want Pietersen to challenge me

metadata.summary: England coach Brendon McCullum wants to be "challenged" by white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen and has "no problem" with the former batter's previous criticism of the team.
metadata.content: England coach Brendon McCullum wants Kevin Pietersen to 'challenge' him, has 'no problem' with previous criticisms | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content England coach Brendon McCullum wants Kevin Pietersen to 'challenge' him, has 'no problem' with previous criticisms Brendon McCullum hopes Kevin Pietersen's "big personality" and "fierce competitiveness" can help England become best white-ball team in the world; KP now a mentor as side build for 2027 50-over World Cup; watch first T20 vs Sri Lanka live on Sky Sports from 6pm Tuesday (6.30pm first ball) Monday 14 September 2026 17:14, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum spoke on Kevin Pietersen becoming a mentor for the side and discussed if previous criticism of the team will affect their relationship England coach Brendon McCullum wants to be "challenged" by white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen and has "no problem" with the former batter's previous criticism of the team. Pietersen will work with England for most series up to and including the 2027 World Cup, starting during the three T20s and as many ODIs at home to Sri Lanka this month. The 46-year-old, who scored almost 14,000 runs across all three formats of international cricket between 2004 and 20144, accused England of a lack of preparation during a white-ball tour of India in 2025 in which they lost ODI and T20I series.
